title: The Fight for (and Against) a $15 Minimum Wage

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯 DealBook 报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is a daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Even as President Biden and congressional Democrats celebrate a historic expansion of the social safety net with the
sentences.zh: 尽管拜登总统和国会民主党人正在庆祝随着刺激法案的通过，

sentences.en: passage of the stimulus bill, they acknowledge that one key policy did not make it in, a doubling of the federal minimum wage to $15 an hour.
sentences.zh: 社会安全网实现了历史性的扩张，但他们也承认，一项关键政策未能纳入其中，即将联邦最低工资提高到每小时15美元。

sentences.en: Today, as Biden vows to do whatever it takes to get to $15, my colleague Shira Frankel spoke with economics reporter Ben Castleman
sentences.zh: 今天，在拜登誓言要不惜一切代价实现15美元目标之际，我的同事希拉·弗兰克尔采访了经济记者本·卡斯尔曼，

sentences.en: about what a growing body of data tells us might happen and might not happen if that occurs.
sentences.zh: 探讨了大量不断增长的数据告诉我们，如果这一目标实现，可能会发生什么，以及可能不会发生什么。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, March 17th.
sentences.zh: 今天是3月17日，星期三。

sentences.en: So Ben, first of all, what's the minimum wage and who earns it?
sentences.zh: 那么本，首先，什么是最低工资，谁在赚取最低工资？

sentences.en: So the federal minimum wage is $7.25 an hour.
sentences.zh: 联邦最低工资是每小时7.25美元。

sentences.en: It's been set at that level since 2009.
sentences.zh: 自2009年以来一直维持在这个水平。

sentences.en: And there are only about 400,000 workers who earn the federal minimum wage.
sentences.zh: 只有大约40万名工人赚取联邦最低工资。

sentences.en: That's in 2019, which is not that many people, in part because it's been so long that many state and local governments have actually gone ahead and raised their own minimum wages.
sentences.zh: 这是2019年的数据，人数并不多，部分原因是由于这个标准已经太久没有调整，许多州和地方政府实际上已经自行提高了最低工资。

sentences.en: But there are still 8 million workers who earn less than $10 an hour, 40 million workers, give or take, who earn less than $15 an hour.
sentences.zh: 但仍有800万工人每小时收入低于10美元，大约4000万工人每小时收入低于15美元。

sentences.en: Many of them work in fast food or cleaning hotel rooMs. Nearly 60% of them are women.
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人从事快餐业或酒店客房清洁工作。其中近60%是女性。

sentences.en: They're disproportionately Black and Hispanic.
sentences.zh: 他们中黑人和拉美裔的比例过高。

sentences.en: They're disproportionately young, although many of them are still over the age of 25.
sentences.zh: 他们中年轻人的比例过高，尽管他们中的许多人已经超过25岁。

sentences.en: Okay, how did we get here?
sentences.zh: 好的，我们是怎么走到这一步的？

sentences.en: Like, take us back to the very beginning of how the federal minimum wage was first established.
sentences.zh: 比如，带我们回到最初，联邦最低工资是如何建立的。

sentences.en: So the first federal minimum wage was passed in 1938.
sentences.zh: 第一个联邦最低工资法案是在1938年通过的。

sentences.en: My friends, five years ago, we faced a very serious problem of economic and social recovery.
sentences.zh: 我的朋友们，五年前，我们面临着非常严重的经济和社会复苏问题。

sentences.en: Under Franklin Delano Roosevelt.
sentences.zh: 在富兰克林·德拉诺·罗斯福领导下。
zh_words: 富兰克林·德拉诺·罗斯福

sentences.en: And it comes out of this moment of the Great Depression.
sentences.zh: 它产生于大萧条时期。

sentences.en: And so we've had this period of just colossal disruption in the American economy, right?
sentences.zh: 我们经历了美国经济中巨大的动荡时期，对吧？

sentences.en: Massive unemployment, incredibly high rates of poverty and suffering.
sentences.zh: 大规模失业，极高的贫困率和苦难。

sentences.en: Consequently, I am again expressing my hope that the Congress will enact at this session a wage and hour bill, putting a floor under industrial wages and a limit on working hours
sentences.zh: 因此，我再次表达我的希望，即国会将在本次会议上颁布一项工资和工时法案，为工业工资设定下限，并限制工作时间，

sentences.en: to ensure a better distribution of our prosperity, a better distribution of available work, and a sounder distribution of buying power.
sentences.zh: 以确保我们的繁荣得到更好的分配，现有工作得到更好的分配，以及购买力得到更合理的分配。

sentences.en: And we get the first push of the New Deal.
sentences.zh: 我们迎来了“新政”的第一次推动。

sentences.en: We get a lot of efforts to try to put people to work, but also to make sure that they are able to make enough money to feed their families.
sentences.zh: 我们做了很多努力来尝试让人们就业，同时也确保他们能够赚到足够的钱来养活家人。

sentences.en: For to reach a port, we must sail.
sentences.zh: 为了到达港口，我们必须航行。

sentences.en: Sail, not lie at anchor.
sentences.zh: 航行，而不是停泊。

sentences.en: Sail, not drift.
sentences.zh: 航行，而不是漂流。

sentences.en: And the minimum wage was initially part of that push, but it got blocked by the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 最低工资最初是该推动计划的一部分，但被最高法院阻止了。

sentences.en: And so it's actually not until 1938 that the federal government is actually able to impose the first minimum wage, which was at the time 25 cents an hour.
sentences.zh: 所以直到1938年，联邦政府才真正能够实施第一个最低工资标准，当时是每小时25美分。

sentences.en: So before 1938, there's just no floor?
sentences.zh: 所以在1938年之前，根本没有下限？

sentences.en: You could literally pay people anything you want?
sentences.zh: 你可以随心所欲地付给人们任何工资？

sentences.en: There's no floor.
sentences.zh: 没有下限。

sentences.en: There were some efforts to have industries regulate wages, but for all intents and purposes, if you could find somebody to work for a given rate, then you could pay them that rate.
sentences.zh: 当时有一些行业监管工资的努力，但实际上，如果你能找到人以给定的费率工作，那么你就可以付给他们那个费率。

sentences.en: And so what was the reaction to the first minimum wage when it was announced?
sentences.zh: 那么，当第一个最低工资标准宣布时，反应如何？

sentences.en: Well, you know, what's interesting is that going back all the way to the start of this, the minimum wage has been just consistently an extremely popular policy.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，有趣的是，追溯到这一切的开始，最低工资一直是一项非常受欢迎的政策。

sentences.en: I found a 1937
sentences.zh: 我发现了一份1937年的

sentences.en: Gallup poll where 69 percent of the public supported a federal minimum wage.
sentences.zh: 盖洛普民意调查，显示69%的公众支持联邦最低工资。

sentences.en: So this is something that has had broad public support basically from the very beginning.
sentences.zh: 所以这基本上从一开始就得到了广泛的公众支持。

sentences.en: So from there, what happens?
sentences.zh: 那么从那时起，发生了什么？

sentences.en: How frequently is the federal minimum wage increased?
sentences.zh: 联邦最低工资多久增加一次？

sentences.en: So it kind of goes up every few years.
sentences.zh: 它每隔几年就会上涨一次。

sentences.en: You know, this was always controlled by Congress.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这总是由国会控制的。

sentences.en: And so it's not like it just automatically rose with the cost of living.
sentences.zh: 所以它并不是随着生活成本自动上涨的。

sentences.en: But, you know, we started with 25 cents an hour in 1938.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，我们从1938年的每小时25美分开始。

sentences.en: That kind of goes up to 30 cents the next year to 40 cents in 45.
sentences.zh: 第二年涨到了30美分，45年涨到了40美分。

sentences.en: We finally crossed to a dollar in 56.
sentences.zh: 我们在56年终于突破了一美元。

sentences.en: By the late 60s, we're at a buck 40 and a buck 60.
sentences.zh: 到了60年代末，我们达到了1.4美元和1.6美元。

sentences.en: And we finally get up to two bucks an hour in 1974.
sentences.zh: 我们最终在1974年达到了每小时2美元。

sentences.en: And then in the 1980s, it kind of stops.
sentences.zh: 然后在80年代，它停滞了。

sentences.en: We get suddenly close to a decade with no increase in the minimum wage.
sentences.zh: 我们突然经历了近十年没有提高最低工资的情况。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: What happens in the 1980s?
sentences.zh: 80年代发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well, I mean, the short version is that Ronald Reagan is elected.
sentences.zh: 嗯，简短的版本是罗纳德·里根当选了。

sentences.en: And we get this sort of conservative revolution where the ideas of the free market are sort of dominant in a lot of
sentences.zh: 我们迎来了某种保守派革命，自由市场的思想在许多

sentences.en: American policymaking.
sentences.zh: 美国决策中占据了主导地位。

sentences.en: There was this argument that it was going to be a job killer.
sentences.zh: 当时有一种论点认为它会成为“就业杀手”。

sentences.en: This is something that you heard from businesses, particularly small businesses, from the very beginning.
sentences.zh: 这是你从一开始就从企业，特别是小企业那里听到的声音。

sentences.en: And it's kind of a natural thing to think, right?
sentences.zh: 这是一种很自然的思考方式，对吧？

sentences.en: If you think about the price for anything else, if you raise the price of bananas or bicycles or iPhones, we would expect demand for that item to fall.
sentences.zh: 如果你考虑任何其他商品的价格，如果你提高香蕉、自行车或iPhone的价格，我们预计对该商品的需求会下降。

sentences.en: And so if we're raising the price of labor, raising the price that you have to pay workers, then you would expect for companies to hire fewer of them.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我们提高劳动力的价格，提高你必须支付给工人的价格，那么你就会预期公司会雇佣更少的人。

sentences.en: And I think that this was a widely held belief, right?
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一种被广泛持有的信念，对吧？

sentences.en: This was not just, you know, some right-wingers or some, you know, hard conservatives who were arguing this.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是一些右翼分子或一些强硬的保守派在争论这个问题。

sentences.en: You know, the New York Times editorial page in 1987, I'm looking at an editorial of theirs right here.
sentences.zh: 你知道，《纽约时报》1987年的社论版，我正在看他们的一篇社论。

sentences.en: The headline is, The Right Minimum Wage, Zero Dollars.
sentences.zh: 标题是《正确的最低工资：零美元》。

sentences.en: That's interesting.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣。

sentences.en: And so the New York Times editorial page is supporting this underlying philosophy that Reagan's introducing.
sentences.zh: 所以《纽约时报》的社论版支持里根引入的这种基本哲学。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, look, so there are two things happening here.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，看，这里有两件事在发生。

sentences.en: There's an ideological moment in America at that point under Reagan, where, you know, this is the era of government isn't the solution, government is the problem.
sentences.zh: 在里根领导下，美国当时正处于一个意识形态时刻，你知道，这是“政府不是解决方案，政府是问题所在”的时代。

sentences.en: But we're also at a time when a lot of economists and not only conservative economists would have said that the minimum wage, if maybe zero
sentences.zh: 但我们也处于这样一个时期，许多经济学家，不仅是保守派经济学家，都会说最低工资，即使零

sentences.en: isn't the right number, but certainly that the too high a minimum wage would carry a real threat to employment and that there were better ways of trying to help the poor.
sentences.zh: 不是正确的数字，但肯定过高的最低工资会对就业构成真正的威胁，而且有更好的方法来帮助穷人。

sentences.en: Remember, this is the 80s, right?
sentences.zh: 记住，这是80年代，对吧？

sentences.en: This is a period of rising inequality.
sentences.zh: 这是一个不平等加剧的时期。

sentences.en: This is a period where for many people, for certainly the wealthy, this was a very good time in the economy.
sentences.zh: 这是一个对许多人，当然对富人来说，经济状况非常好的时期。

sentences.en: But there was the beginnings of these fears of inequality that we're now seeing.
sentences.zh: 但我们现在看到的不平等恐惧已经开始萌芽。

sentences.en: And I think you can certainly link that back in part to this stagnation of the minimum wage during that period.
sentences.zh: 我认为你当然可以将此部分归因于那一时期最低工资的停滞。

sentences.en: So what happens after the Reagan years in the 90s and the early 2000s?
sentences.zh: 那么在里根时代之后的90年代和21世纪初发生了什么？

sentences.en: You know, we got some increases under Clinton.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们在克林顿执政期间获得了一些增长。

sentences.en: We got some increases under George W.
sentences.zh: 我们在乔治·W·布什执政期间也获得了一些增长。

sentences.en: Bush.
sentences.zh: 但自2009年以来，最低工资一直停滞不前。

sentences.en: But then the minimum wage has stalled since 2009.
sentences.zh: 上一位真正通过国会提高最低工资的总统是乔治·W·布什。

sentences.en: The last president to actually get a minimum wage increase through Congress was George W.
sentences.zh: 那是，你知道，正值大衰退时期，这是自大萧条以来最严重的衰退。

sentences.en: Bush.
sentences.zh: 之后我们经历了非常漫长而痛苦的复苏，在很大程度上，低薪工人并没有看到任何工资增长。

sentences.en: That was, you know, right in the teeth of the Great Recession, the worst recession since the Great Depression.
sentences.zh: 然后我们在最后终于迎来了失业率低、经济好转、工资上涨的时期，但最低工资工人仍然没有受益。

sentences.en: We then get this very long, tortured recovery from that where for much of it, low wage workers are really not seeing any wage gains.
sentences.zh: 当然，过去一年我们经历了疫情。

sentences.en: And then we finally get this period at the end of it when the unemployment rate is low and the economy is doing better and wages are rising, but still not for minimum wage workers.
sentences.zh: 所以这对经济来说是了不起的十年多。

sentences.en: And then, of course, for the past year, we've had the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 但对于最低工资工人来说，他们在这期间没有获得任何收益。

sentences.en: So it's been a remarkable decade plus for the economy.
sentences.zh: 在这一切之下，从2012年开始，出现了一场草根运动，工会的进步活动人士推动的不仅仅是更高的

sentences.en: But for minimum wage workers, they've seen none of the gains during that period.
sentences.zh: 联邦最低工资，而是翻倍，甚至超过翻倍，达到每小时15美元，这就是后来被称为“为15美元而战”的运动。

sentences.en: Underneath all of that, starting in 2012, there's this grassroots movement, progressive activists of unions to push for not just a higher
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: federal minimum wage, but a doubling, a more than doubling of the minimum wage to $15 an hour, what became known as the fight for $15.

sentences.zh: 解锁？

sentences.zh: 一个月的时间让你深入了解《时报》订阅者每天都能获得的内容。

sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 本，人们对“为15美元而战”的草根运动有什么看法？

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我可以告诉你我的想法。

sentences.en: Ben, what did people think about the grassroots movement for the fight for $15?
sentences.zh: 当时我是《华尔街日报》报道经济的记者。

sentences.en: Well, I can tell you what I thought.
sentences.zh: 2012年，我开始收到关于麦当劳最低工资工人罢工要求提高工资的新闻稿。

sentences.en: I was a reporter at the Wall Street Journal at the time covering the economy.
sentences.zh: 我开始看到示威和抗议活动。

sentences.en: And in 2012, I started to get press releases about minimum wage workers who were walking out to demand higher pay at McDonald's.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我当时对此相当不屑一顾。

sentences.en: I started seeing demonstrations and protests.
sentences.zh: 我想很多经济记者也是这样。

sentences.en: And I'll be honest, I was pretty dismissive of it at the time.
sentences.zh: 首先，因为它在政治上似乎是不可能的。

sentences.en: I think a lot of economics reporters were.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是一个连

sentences.en: For one thing, because it just seemed politically impossible.
sentences.zh: 民主党人都不太支持15美元最低工资的时刻。

sentences.en: You know, this is a moment when even
sentences.zh: 你知道，奥巴马总统当时谈论的是将最低工资大幅提高到10.10美元。

sentences.en: Democrats were not remotely on board with a minimum wage of $15.
sentences.zh: 就在2016年的总统竞选中，希拉里·克林顿还在谈论12美元的最低工资。

sentences.en: You know, President Obama was talking about a huge increase in the minimum wage to $10.10.
sentences.zh: 她在全国范围内并不支持15美元的最低工资。

sentences.en: And as recently as 2016, in the presidential campaign, Hillary Clinton was talking about a $12 minimum wage.
sentences.zh: 所以当时并没有实现这一目标的政治时机。

sentences.en: She wasn't on board with a $15 minimum wage nationally.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这也是当时的传统智慧，认为这对经济来说负担太重了。

sentences.en: So the political moment just wasn't there for this to happen.
sentences.zh: 在联邦层面设定那么高的最低工资的想法，我认为对许多

sentences.en: But I think it was also the conventional wisdom that this would be much too much for the economy.
sentences.zh: 经济学家来说似乎很疯狂，坦率地说，可能对我们当时报道这件事的许多人来说也是如此。

sentences.en: That the notion of setting a minimum wage that high at the federal level just seemed crazy, I think, to a lot of
sentences.zh: 那么他们为什么选择15美元？

sentences.en: economists and frankly, probably to a lot of us who were covering it at the time.
sentences.zh: 嗯，草根阶层的论点是，15美元是真正拥有生活工资所必需的。

sentences.en: So why did they land on $15?
sentences.zh: 这是一种认为最低工资应该是一个你真正能赖以生存的工资的论点。

sentences.en: Well, so the argument among the grassroots was that $15 was what it took to actually have a living wage.
sentences.zh: 他们想出了15美元作为一个合理的数字。

sentences.en: It was this argument that the minimum wage ought to be a wage that you could actually live on.
sentences.zh: 看，这也是一个朗朗上口的整数。

sentences.en: And they came up with $15 as a reasonable number for that.
sentences.zh: 我不认为“为15美元而战”比“为14.85美元而战”或算法可能吐出的任何数字作为口号更好，这有什么神秘之处。

sentences.en: Look, it's also a catchy round number.
sentences.zh: 但核心思想是最低工资应该是一个生活工资。

sentences.en: I don't think, you know, there's any mystery that the fight for $15 was a better slogan than, you know, fight for $14.85 or whatever the algorithm might have spit out.
sentences.zh: 所以除了押韵好听之外，他们做了什么来说服像你这样的人这是一个好主意？

sentences.en: But the idea was that the minimum wage ought to be a living wage.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，“为15美元而战”运动在早期做了几件事。

sentences.en: So other than the alliteration being good, what did they do to convince people like you that this was a good idea?
sentences.zh: 他们做的一件事是对个别公司施加了很大压力。

sentences.en: Well, you know, the fight for $15 movement did a couple of things early on.
sentences.zh: 他们说麦当劳应该有能力支付更多。

sentences.en: One thing they did is they put a lot of pressure on individual companies.
sentences.zh: 沃尔玛应该有能力支付更多。

sentences.en: They said McDonald's ought to be able to pay more.
sentences.zh: 让我们对他们施加政治压力，要求他们提高工资。

sentences.en: Walmart ought to be able to pay more.
sentences.zh: 位于奥克布鲁克的麦当劳总部是“为15美元而战”最低工资斗争的中心。

sentences.en: Let's put political pressure on them to raise their pay.
sentences.zh: 数百名抗议者在那里搭帐篷过夜。

sentences.en: The McDonald's headquarters in Oakbrook is ground zero for the fight for $15 minimum wage battle.
sentences.zh: 今天早上，他们也希望影响麦当劳的股东。

sentences.en: Hundreds of protesters spent the night there in tents.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，他们在州和地方层面进行了大量的斗争。

sentences.en: And this morning, they're also hoping to influence McDonald's shareholders.
sentences.zh: 在旧金山，美国消费最高的城市之一。

sentences.en: And at the same time, they did a lot of fighting at the state and local level.
sentences.zh: 包括旧金山和西雅图在内的几个美国主要城市已经批准了最低工资增长。

sentences.en: In San Francisco, one of the most expensive cities in America.
sentences.zh: 几个美国主要城市，包括旧金山和西雅图，已经批准了最低工资增长。

sentences.en: Several major U.S.
sentences.zh: 几个美国主要城市，包括旧金山和西雅图，已经批准了最低工资增长。

sentences.en: cities, including San Francisco and Seattle, have approved minimum wage increases.
sentences.zh: 几个美国主要城市，包括旧金山和西雅图，已经批准了最低工资增长。

sentences.en: Others, such as New York City and Washington, D.C., are considering them now.
sentences.zh: 其他城市，比如纽约市和华盛顿特区，现在也在考虑中。

sentences.en: And so, at first, this experiment is mostly playing out in some high cost of living, sort of progressive cities.
sentences.zh: 所以起初，这项实验主要是在一些生活成本高、相对进步的城市中进行。

sentences.en: But then it starts to spread.
sentences.zh: 但随后它开始蔓延开来。

sentences.en: In 2016, California, the whole state, so not just San Francisco, but Fresno and the Central Valley, gets a higher minimum wage.
sentences.zh: 2016年，加利福尼亚州全州——不仅仅是旧金山，还包括弗雷斯诺和中央谷地——都提高了最低工资标准。

sentences.en: In 2016, Arizona voters vote on a minimum wage bill.
sentences.zh: 2016年，亚利桑那州的选民对一项最低工资法案进行了投票。

sentences.en: Illinois votes on a minimum wage bill.
sentences.zh: 伊利诺伊州也对最低工资法案进行了投票。

sentences.en: And eventually, by the time we get to the present day, there are 28 states, plus the District of Columbia, that have raised their minimum wage since January of
sentences.zh: 最终，到了今天，自2014年1月以来，已经有28个州加上哥伦比亚特区提高了最低工资。

sentences.en: And so, as you might imagine, economists rushed in to study this.
sentences.zh: 所以，正如你所料，经济学家们纷纷涌入研究这一课题。

sentences.en: And as you also might expect, if you've ever paid attention to economists, they don't all agree with each other.
sentences.zh: 正如你可能预料到的，如果你关注过经济学家，就会发现他们之间并不总是意见一致。

sentences.en: But I think that there is sort of a broad takeaway from the studies that have been done, which is that the damage of
sentences.zh: 但我认为，从已有的研究中可以得出一个大致的结论，那就是

sentences.en: these higher minimum wages is not nearly as significant as many people feared.
sentences.zh: 这些提高后的最低工资所带来的负面影响，远没有许多人担心的那么严重。

sentences.en: Some of these studies find basically no job losses from these higher minimum wages.
sentences.zh: 一些研究发现，提高最低工资基本上没有导致失业。

sentences.en: Some of them find modest job loss, but generally not of the kind of disastrous scale that we might have predicted.
sentences.zh: 另一些研究发现会有适度的失业，但通常没有达到我们可能预期的那种灾难性规模。

sentences.en: And at the same time, these higher minimum wages bring real benefits for those workers.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，这些更高的最低工资确实为那些工人带来了实实在在的好处。

sentences.en: They are bringing higher pay.
sentences.zh: 他们获得了更高的报酬。

sentences.en: They're bringing higher pay not just for the workers earning the minimum wage, but also for workers who are earning a bit more than that, who can now go to their managers and say,
sentences.zh: 不仅是领取最低工资的工人获得了更高的报酬，那些收入稍高一点的工人也因此受益，他们现在可以去跟经理说：

sentences.en: come on, that 16-year-old is earning the minimum wage.
sentences.zh: 拜托，那个16岁的孩子都拿最低工资了。

sentences.en: Like, you're not going to pay me the same as him.
sentences.zh: 你总不能给我开得跟他一样吧。

sentences.en: And so, we are seeing this play out in the form of these higher wages without the sort of disastrous consequences that I think a lot of people would have predicted.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们看到这种情况以工资上涨的形式呈现出来，并没有出现我认为许多人预期的那种灾难性后果。

sentences.en: But when all the workers are getting a raise, even beyond the lowest wage workers to a broader set of people, how can that not be bad for business?
sentences.zh: 但当所有工人都加薪时，甚至超出了最低工资工人，惠及更广泛的人群，这怎么可能对企业不利呢？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: I mean, I think it's a good question, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得这是一个好问题，对吧？

sentences.en: Because we talked earlier about that sort of idea of a simple supply and demand market.
sentences.zh: 因为我们之前讨论过那种简单的供需市场理念。

sentences.en: If we raise the costs for employers, how could they not need to cut workers?
sentences.zh: 如果我们增加了雇主的成本，他们怎么可能不需要裁员呢？

sentences.en: And I think that the answer is that there's a growing body of evidence that the real world does not work the way that simple supply and demand model suggests.
sentences.zh: 我认为答案是，越来越多的证据表明，现实世界并不像简单的供需模型所暗示的那样运作。

sentences.en: So, let me give an example of that.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我举个例子。

sentences.en: If my labor is worth, call it, eight bucks an hour, and my employer tries to pay me only $7.25, in a simple supply and demand model, I'm not going to keep that $7.25 job.
sentences.zh: 如果我的劳动力价值，比如说每小时8美元，而我的雇主只试图付给我7.25美元，在简单的供需模型中，我是不会留在这个7.25美元的工作岗位上的。

sentences.en: I'm going to walk out the door and find somebody who'll pay me eight bucks an hour.
sentences.zh: 我会直接走人，去找一个愿意付我每小时8美元的人。

sentences.en: I'd be crazy to stick around.
sentences.zh: 如果我留下来那才叫疯了。

sentences.en: But in the real world, it can be more complicated than that.
sentences.zh: 但在现实世界中，情况可能比这复杂得多。

sentences.en: It might feel really risky for me to quit my job.
sentences.zh: 辞职对我来说可能感觉风险很大。

sentences.en: It might be really hard for me to pick up and move across town for the job that pays me $8 an hour.
sentences.zh: 为了那份每小时8美元的工作而搬到城另一边，对我来说可能非常困难。

sentences.en: Or maybe I don't know that my real worth is eight bucks an hour, and my employer is paying me $7.25, and I think that that's just what the market will bear.
sentences.zh: 或者我可能不知道我的真实价值是每小时8美元，而雇主只付我7.25美元，我还以为这就是市场行情。

sentences.en: And so, there are a lot of different ways in which employers can end up paying workers less than that simple supply and demand model might suggest they ought to.
sentences.zh: 所以，雇主最终支付给工人的工资低于简单供需模型所暗示的水平，这种情况有很多种原因。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So, actually, workers and companies don't shift around as much and as easily as economists thought they would.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，工人和公司之间的流动并没有经济学家想象的那么频繁和容易。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But I should add that we've been talking here as if the only potential cost of the minimum wage is lost jobs.
sentences.zh: 但我得补充一点，我们刚才的讨论好像把最低工资的唯一潜在成本当成了失业。

sentences.en: And it's more complicated than that, too.
sentences.zh: 但情况比这复杂得多。

sentences.en: There are ways that the minimum wage could play out in the real world that has other potentially negative effects.
sentences.zh: 最低工资在现实世界中可能会产生其他潜在的负面影响。

sentences.en: So, for example, it may be that we keep the same number of jobs in total, but it becomes harder for teenagers to get
sentences.zh: 例如，可能总的就业岗位数量保持不变，但青少年变得更难找到

sentences.en: jobs because if I'm going to have to pay $15 an hour, I'm not going to hire some 16-year-old to do the work.
sentences.zh: 工作了，因为如果我必须支付每小时15美元的工资，我就不会雇佣一个16岁的孩子来干活。

sentences.en: Or the minimum wage could be more damaging for small businesses than for large businesses because the bigger businesses are in a better position to pay those higher wages.
sentences.zh: 或者，最低工资对小企业造成的损害可能比大企业更大，因为大企业更有能力支付这些更高的工资。

sentences.en: So, it's been notable during this recent debate, for example, that Amazon not only came out a few
sentences.zh: 所以，在最近的这场辩论中，值得注意的是，例如，亚马逊不仅在几

sentences.en: years ago and said that they were going to start paying at least $15 an hour to all their workers,
sentences.zh: 年前就宣布他们将开始向所有员工支付至少每小时15美元的工资，

sentences.en: but they've also come out and been advertising heavily and lobbying heavily in favor of a $15 an hour minimum wage.
sentences.zh: 而且他们还公开进行了大量的广告宣传和游说，支持每小时15美元的最低工资。

sentences.en: And there are a lot of small businesses that see that and get a little suspicious, that say, if Amazon is for this, that can't possibly be good news for small businesses.
sentences.zh: 很多小企业看到这一点会感到有些怀疑，他们会说，如果亚马逊都支持这个，那对小企业来说绝不可能是好消息。

sentences.en: And maybe this is basically a way for Amazon and for other big companies to gain yet another advantage over smaller businesses that are already struggling to compete.
sentences.zh: 也许这基本上是亚马逊和其他大公司获得相对于已经在苦苦挣扎的小企业又一项优势的手段。

sentences.en: And we still have not seen these kinds of higher minimum wages in most of the truly low-income, low-cost-of-living parts of the country.
sentences.zh: 而且，在全国大多数真正低收入、低生活成本的地区，我们还没有看到这种提高最低工资的情况。

sentences.en: And to the extent that we have, we don't have a lot of evidence from those places yet because the increases have been recent.
sentences.zh: 即便有，我们也还没有从这些地方获得太多证据，因为这些增长是最近才发生的。

sentences.en: So, I think that there are still questions out there about how this plays out as it rolls out across the country.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为关于这套方案在全国范围内推广时会如何演变，仍然存在疑问。

sentences.en: But I do think that it is safe to say that the weight of the evidence has shifted and that the weight of the views of economists have shifted with it.
sentences.zh: 但我认为可以肯定地说，证据的权重已经发生了转移，经济学家的观点权重也随之发生了转移。

sentences.en: If we were having this conversation 20 or maybe even 10 years ago, I think the conversation we'd be
sentences.zh: 如果我们是在20年前，甚至可能是10年前进行这次谈话，我想我们当时

sentences.en: having was about how economists thought this was a terrible idea and would be hugely damaging, even if it was popular in the public.
sentences.zh: 讨论的会是经济学家如何认为这是一个糟糕的主意，会造成巨大的破坏，即使它在公众中很受欢迎。

sentences.en: And the conversation that we're having now is much more nuanced.
sentences.zh: 而我们现在进行的谈话则要微妙得多。

sentences.en: It's, yes, there may be some costs, but there are also some benefits.
sentences.zh: 那就是，是的，可能会有一些成本，但也有一些好处。

sentences.en: Some economists will argue those costs are larger, others smaller, but it's not this sort of consensus view that this is a bad idea that it once was.
sentences.zh: 一些经济学家会争辩说成本更大，另一些则认为更小，但这不再是那种“这是一个坏主意”的共识了。

sentences.en: So, I'm wondering if the political thinking has also shifted on this.
sentences.zh: 所以我很好奇，政治上的想法是否也发生了转变。

sentences.en: Yeah, the politics of this have shifted maybe even more dramatically than the economics.
sentences.zh: 是的，这方面的政治立场转变可能比经济学上的转变更为剧烈。

sentences.en: If you think back to earlier when I said that Hillary Clinton did not support a $15 minimum wage when she was running
sentences.zh: 如果你回想一下我之前说的，希拉里·克林顿在2016年参选时并不支持15美元的最低工资，

sentences.en: in 2016, in 2020, virtually every major Democratic candidate was advocating for a $15 minimum wage.
sentences.zh: 到了2020年，几乎每一位主要的民主党候选人都在主张15美元的最低工资。

sentences.en: And of course, Biden, who, you know, was the sort of moderate in the field, has come in and has been pushing for a
sentences.zh: 当然，拜登，你知道，他是党内相对温和派，上任后也一直在推动

sentences.en: $15 minimum wage.
sentences.zh: 15美元的最低工资。

sentences.en: So there has been this dramatic shift where it was kind of a fringe idea, even among
sentences.zh: 所以发生了这种巨大的转变，它从一种边缘思想，即使在

sentences.en: Democrats, to being very much the mainstream position of the Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 民主党内部，变成了民主党非常主流的立场。

sentences.en: But mainstream does not mean that it has the votes necessary to get there.
sentences.zh: 但主流并不意味着它拥有实现这一目标所需的选票。

sentences.en: And what we saw in the Senate recently is that there still are not the crucial 50 Democratic votes to push a $15 minimum wage across the finish line.
sentences.zh: 我们最近在参议院看到的是，仍然没有关键的50张民主党选票来推动15美元的最低工资跨过终点线。

sentences.en: So, what about the Republicans?
sentences.zh: 那么共和党人呢？

sentences.en: The Republican discussion is more complicated.
sentences.zh: 共和党的讨论更为复杂。

sentences.en: There is certainly some support in the Republican caucus for raising the minimum wage.
sentences.zh: 在共和党核心小组中，确实有一些支持提高最低工资的声音。

sentences.en: Mitt Romney and Tom Cotton, two Republican senators, came out earlier this year for an increase in the minimum wage up to $10 over four years.
sentences.zh: 米特·罗姆尼和汤姆·科顿，两位共和党参议员，今年早些时候提出在四年内将最低工资提高到10美元。

sentences.en: But there are still a lot of Republicans in Congress who are, in some cases, outright opposed to even the
sentences.zh: 但国会中仍有许多共和党人，在某些情况下，他们甚至直接反对

sentences.en: idea of a federal minimum wage or who certainly don't think that it should be raised quickly.
sentences.zh: 联邦最低工资的概念，或者肯定认为不应该快速提高。

sentences.en: That sort of Reagan influence remains in place.
sentences.zh: 那种里根时代的影响依然存在。

sentences.en: So if President Biden and the Democrats decide that ultimately, in the face of immigration reform, climate policies, solving COVID and all the other
sentences.zh: 所以，如果拜登总统和民主党人最终决定，面对移民改革、气候政策、解决新冠疫情以及所有其他

sentences.en: priorities they have, this isn't going to be their legislative priority.
sentences.zh: 他们优先考虑的事项，这不会成为他们的立法重点。

sentences.en: What is going to happen to the federal minimum wage?
sentences.zh: 联邦最低工资会发生什么？

sentences.en: Are we going to keep having states raising their wage in keeping with the cost of
sentences.zh: 我们是否会继续看到各州根据生活成本提高工资，私营公司决定逐步提高最低工资，

sentences.en: living, private companies deciding to raise their minimum wage incrementally, but the federal government just staying out of this argument?
sentences.zh: 而联邦政府却置身事外？

sentences.en: It's a great question, and it's a hard one to answer.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的问题，也是一个很难回答的问题。

sentences.en: I think we will continue to see this push at the state and local level.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们将继续看到这种在州和地方层面的推动。

sentences.en: I think we'll continue to see the push at the private industry level.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们将继续看到在私营行业层面的推动。

sentences.en: But look, there are some states that are just not going to raise their minimum wages.
sentences.zh: 但听着，有些州就是不会提高最低工资。

sentences.en: And in fact, there are states that are blocking more progressive cities in those states from raising their minimum wages.
sentences.zh: 事实上，有些州正在阻止州内更进步的城市提高最低工资。

sentences.en: So at the end of the day, the federal policy still matters.
sentences.zh: 所以归根结底，联邦政策仍然很重要。

sentences.en: You know, it's interesting.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这很有趣。

sentences.en: This is such a partisan issue among elected officials.
sentences.zh: 在民选官员中，这是一个非常党派化的议题。

sentences.en: But it's not that partisan among the public.
sentences.zh: 但在公众中，它并没有那么强的党派色彩。

sentences.en: You know, Florida voters in November voted for Donald Trump, as we all know.
sentences.zh: 你知道，佛罗里达州的选民在11月投票给了唐纳德·特朗普，我们都知道。

sentences.en: But they also voted to raise the minimum wage there.
sentences.zh: 但他们同时也投票支持提高那里的最低工资。

sentences.en: And there are a number of polls out there that show not just that a majority of Americans support a $15 minimum wage, but that a significant share of Republicans, in some
sentences.zh: 有很多民意调查显示，不仅大多数美国人支持15美元的最低工资，而且相当大比例的共和党人，在某些

sentences.en: cases a majority of Republicans, support a much higher federal minimum wage than we have right now.
sentences.zh: 情况下甚至是大多数共和党人，都支持比我们现在高得多的联邦最低工资。

sentences.en: So the politics of this are not as simple as they might first appear.
sentences.zh: 所以这背后的政治并不像最初看起来那么简单。

sentences.en: But I think that there is a real possibility that progressives will hold out for 15, and that
sentences.zh: 但我认为，进步派坚持要求15美元，而

sentences.en: moderates will not come around to that number, and that there's a stalemate, and that the result is
sentences.zh: 温和派不会接受这个数字，从而导致僵局，结果是

sentences.en: that we stall out, and that we remain in a place where a worker in America can work 40 hours a week,
sentences.zh: 我们陷入停滞，依然处于一个美国工人每周工作40小时，

sentences.en: 52 weeks a year, and earn only $15,000.
sentences.zh: 一年工作52周，却只能赚15000美元的境地。

sentences.en: That's the world that we're in right now, and with each passing year, it gets even harder to get by on that wage.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们现在的世界，随着一年年过去，靠这份工资生活变得越来越难。

sentences.en: Thank you, Ben.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，本。

sentences.en: Thanks so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine, until this summer, when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
